claims.text: Substituting heavy elements with light elements such as Al and Ti enables low density in lightweight HEAs.
Light-element substitution combined with high configurational entropy produces a highly homogeneous, disordered solid solution.
Atomic disorder and lattice distortion hinder dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
A homogeneous disordered structure promotes continuous protective passivation and thus improves corrosion resistance.
A homogeneous solid-solution structure promotes a continuous protective oxide and thus improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Phase segregation or secondary-phase precipitation lowers the mechanical strength of lightweight HEAs.
Elemental segregation degrades the corrosion resistance of lightweight HEAs.
Phase segregation or secondary-phase precipitation increases high-temperature oxidation rates.
AlCrTiV can serve as a homogeneous, single-phase lightweight HEA when produced by controlled magnetron sputtering or vacuum arc melting.
Changing processing conditions or composition can deliberately induce local segregation or secondary-phase formation in the baseline alloy.
The homogeneous single-phase structure contains a uniformly distributed lattice-strain field arising from random atomic-scale disorder.
High mixing entropy enforces chemical uniformity in the alloy.
Chemical homogeneity minimizes corrosion-active sites.
Uniform availability of Al or Cr forms and maintains continuous, adherent protective surface films.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, an alloy with induced segregation or secondary phases will have lower yield strength.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, an alloy with induced segregation will have higher corrosion current density or lower polarization resistance.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, an alloy with induced segregation or secondary phases will exhibit greater oxidation mass gain at about 900 °C.
The homogeneous structure is typically stable during mechanical testing at room or moderately elevated temperatures.
The comparison should use a homogeneous control and an intentionally inhomogeneous experimental alloy and measure strength, electrochemical corrosion, and oxidation behavior.
A lack of statistically significant deterioration in strength, corrosion resistance, or oxidation resistance in the inhomogeneous alloy would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis explicitly predicts that segregation or secondary phases cause performance deterioration, whereas the boundary says the hypothesis ceases to hold once segregation or secondary phases occur. Those conditions are part of the proposed causal test rather than a clear limit outside its scope.

The intervention permits slight compositional changes, while the experiment initially requires identical nominal compositions but later again refers to modified compositional parameters. It is therefore unclear whether composition is controlled or varied.
